# `begin_streaming`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Image socket: start a live-view frame stream for the requesting client.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build matches (READ)) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, imager binary image table (serves 4800/4804), handler @0x115000 (64-bit build), @0xa5210 (32-bit build); static analysis of app 3.3.2, MainFileManager.startStream; handler signature begin_streaming(int,int,const json_value*,socket_json_imager_server_binary*); subscriber std::map; GetViewMode/GetExpMode; CMyThread::Start on FocusStreamingThread (500 ms new-frame wait; "reponse error, erased" on write failure) |

Image-socket (4800/4804) method. Accepted only in continuous exposure; otherwise the reply is the error text `only available for continuous exposure`. On success the handler registers the calling connection with its request id in the shared stream-subscriber list (under a lock), replies with the text `done`, and starts the live-view streaming thread. That thread waits up to 500 ms for each new preview frame and pushes one framed image per new frame to every registered connection, reusing that connection's request id: JPEG in Jpg mode, otherwise uncompressed raw (dataType 2). A connection whose write fails is dropped from the stream. READ. It mutates shared streaming state and starts a thread: MUTATOR / tier C. The 32-bit build matches (READ). Firmware 9.75 (64-bit): when the preview setting raw_bin2 is true, raw 16-bit Bayer (imgType 1) and RGB48 (imgType 5) frames on the non-JPEG path are binned 2x2 before sending; the header width, height and bytes 20 to 23 are halved and imgType is unchanged (READ; 32-bit not checked).

Side effects: Registers the client in the shared stream-subscriber list under a mutex and starts the live-view streaming thread; reads the current view and exposure modes. A client whose write fails is removed from the list. READ.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"begin_streaming"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Not read by the handler. The app sends no params member. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ] |

## Errors

None. Failures appear in the payload (`code`, `error`) when `state` is `fail`.

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":1,"method":"begin_streaming"}
```
